chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hajjaj, from Thalabah, from Muhammad ibn Mudarrib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to the sale of 'adhrah (a type of small fish or dried fish)."

key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: Adhrah (a type of small fish or dried fish)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell 'adhrah (dried fish) in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility (juz') of selling 'adhrah, a specific type of fish or dried fish, indicating that there are no specific legal impediments to this transaction in Islamic jurisprudence. It reflects the practical application of the general principle that fish are permissible to sell even if not yet caught, provided the species is known and edible, aligning with the Shia view on conditional sales (bay' al-mawjud bi-bay' al-ma'lum).
